subject.title: feat(durable): add beta3 runtime core foundation

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this local durable agent/session runtime as a permanent core architecture, and if so must it use the canonical shared-state/Kysely migration owner before the stacked series proceeds?
rationale: The choice adds permanent core persistence, protocol, CLI, recovery, delivery, and environment contracts; automation cannot decide whether that product architecture is wanted or whether a second database owner is acceptable.

options.title: Adopt through canonical state ownership
options.body: Sponsor the durable-core direction, require the tables and transactions to move behind the existing shared-state/Kysely boundary, then require exact-head upgrade and runtime proof.

options.title: Accept the beta prototype boundary
options.body: Explicitly accept the separate raw-SQL migration owner and operator surfaces for the beta line, with maintainers owning the compatibility and integrity risk.

options.title: Pause the durable stack
options.body: Hold or close the stacked implementation until maintainers approve a narrower architecture and proof plan in the prerequisite RFC.

recommendation.title: Adopt through canonical state ownership
recommendation.body: Sponsor the durable-core direction, require the tables and transactions to move behind the existing shared-state/Kysely boundary, then require exact-head upgrade and runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current shared-state and adjacent durable Gateway architecture on main, so he is best positioned to decide the permanent core boundary.
